$comment: Golden HMAC vectors for src/verify/verifySignature.ts. Generated with the same algorithm as the emitter (backend/app/Webhooks/Domain/Service/HmacSignatureGenerator.php): HMAC-SHA256 over `<unix>.<rawBody>`, rendered as lowercase hex. Secrets here are synthetic fixtures and never existed in any environment.
verifiedAgainstEmitter: 2026-09-02: every header below was recomputed by instantiating HmacSignatureGenerator from the Factuarea monorepo and calling sign() with the same secret, body and instant. Three of the four came back byte for byte identical; tampered_single is DELIBERATELY one hex digit away from the emitter output, which is what makes it a rejection vector.

vectors.name: valid_single
vectors.description: One candidate, signed with the secret the node holds. The verifier must accept it.

vectors.name: tampered_single
vectors.description: The same delivery with one byte of the signature altered. The verifier must reject it with no_match.

vectors.name: rotation_second_matches
vectors.description: Rotation grace window: the emitter signs with the current secret and with the previous one. The node holds the SECOND of the two, so a verifier that reads the first candidate and stops rejects a legitimate delivery.

vectors.name: reserialisation_changes_bytes
vectors.description: The signed body carries \uXXXX escapes, which is what this emitter really sends: RecordEventCommandHandler passes JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES and not JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE, so non-ASCII is escaped and the solidus is not. It also carries escaped solidus, which is json_encode's DEFAULT rather than this emitter's output, kept because a verifier that survives the wider case survives the real one. JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(rawBody)) unescapes both and therefore changes the bytes: verification must accept the raw body and reject the reserialised one.
